title: Prove throw-blocking write guard in a live OpenCode session
action: Hand-write the minimal .opencode/plugins/bee-guard.ts: an async Plugin export whose tool.execute.before maps write/edit/bash tool payloads onto `.bee/bin/bee hook write-guard` stdin payloads and throws an Error carrying the guard's deny message when the guard denies; no rule logic in TypeScript. Then run a live opencode session in this checkout and prove: (a) a guard-denied write (secret-shaped or unreserved guarded target) is refused via the thrown Error, (b) an allowed write on a plain file passes, (c) bee skills are discovered by the session, (d) the AGENTS.md preamble loads. Append the transcript excerpts and the verified layout names to discovery.md — these feed S2.

truths: The plugin holds zero guard rules — every decision comes from .bee/bin/bee hook write-guard
A crash or missing bee binary throws (fail-closed), shown in the plugin code path
Deny and allow transcript excerpts are both recorded in discovery.md
Skills discovery and AGENTS.md load are recorded facts from the live session
